latest_evidence.probe: Test whether a dedicated second Git ref updated only with non-force fast-forward semantics can serve as the independent O(1) anchor for protocol-compliant scheduled-Chat writers, then separately model a force-capable writer.
latest_evidence.result: CONDITIONAL_PROTOCOL_SAFETY_ONLY; TWO_REFS_DO_NOT_ELIMINATE_SHARED_CAS. Non-force fast-forward rejects a stale divergent sibling writer after another writer advances the shared data ref. A surviving cross-linked second ref detects one-ref rewrite. But the data ref remains a shared serialization point, separate REST updates create a torn-update window, and a force-capable actor can coherently rewind both mutable refs to erase later-visible evidence.

frontier: Non-force fast-forward is sufficient to reject stale divergent sibling writers under protocol compliance but does not remove the shared ref serialization point.
A second cross-linked mutable ref adds O(1) conditional one-ref rollback detection but separate REST updates are not an atomic pair.
Coherent force rewind of both refs defeats exact historical rollback detection without an independently monotonic authority/retention domain.
Atomic multi-ref beforeOid CAS is the next highest-value candidate for removing torn updates and partial protocol commits, subject to scheduled-Chat callability and zero-quota verification.
